doc.title: Roswell Rudd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: Customs house job and a cold-water flat
summary: Aged about 25 he worked as a customs house messenger and lived cheaply near Broad Street while studying.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You were about 25 at that time?
Was it hard to live in New York at that time? What were you doing to sustain yourself?

The first job I had when I got to New York was a customs house messenger. I found a cold water flat, $15 a month, on an old block right around the corner from the customs house, before they tore that down and put a bank there. I was on the lowest part of Broad Street, right down on the waterfront, and I would get up, do the day thing, and the rest of the time just play, follow these other guys around, and study. I did that for a couple of years anyway.
